title: Installation Almanac: Week of May 11 2026
content:
Purpose:
A compact weekly ledger for on‑prem/VPC installs and field engineering notes. Mix of standup captures, decisions, and ad hoc troubleshooting that will feed into the formal runbook updates next sprint.

When:
- Week snapshot created 2026-05-11. Notes captured across standups and customer touchpoints (PDT/APAC overlap).

Attendees (rolling across meetings):
- Marcus Li (owner)
- Priya Nair (field lead)
- Ethan Cole (networking)
- Sara Kim (ops/automation)
- Luis Ortega (SRE)
- Customer contacts: Jenna (Acadia Health), Mark (KiteCorp)

High-level summary:
- Two active installs in parallel: Acadia (onprem air-gapped single-rack) and KiteCorp (VPC, multi-subnet). Both at day-two to day-five cadence.
- Acadia: NFS mount flakiness surfaced after warmstart; currently mitigated by failover to local disk + background sync.
- KiteCorp: IPSec tunnel MTU mismatch causing tail latency spikes for grpc calls to the control plane. BFD disabled as temporary mitigation.
- No SLA-impacting outages this week; visible latency jitter on a subset of customer requests (p95 token latency up ~40ms for Acadia daytime runs).

Standup snippets / rapid notes:
- 2026-05-11 09:00 PDT (Field):
  - Acadia: observed frequent ephemeral mount timeouts on node-storage-02. Ops switched to async writeback on that node; background rsync scheduled overnight.
  - Action: Priya to collect dmesg + mount logs and upload to the shared diagnostic folder.
- 2026-05-11 11:30 PDT (Network deep-dive):
  - KiteCorp: IPSec path has 1400 MTU on customer edge, our tunnel endpoint allowed 1500 — fragmentation observed.
  - Decision: Insert path MTU clamp at the proxy (HAProxy set-window-adjust) and roll to canary (1 zone) to measure.
  - Action: Ethan to open DEPLOY-418 and coordinate with customer netops for packet captures.
- 2026-05-12 07:45 PDT (Ops bridge):
  - KV-cache priming for the Acadia deployment delayed after restart due to aggressive cold-start batching.
  - Mitigation: lower initial batch size and pre-warm top-5 prefixes via synthetic traffic generator.
  - Action: Sara to add a short prewarm job to the installer and test in staging.

Customer escalations and context:
- Acadia Health (priority): Customer is sensitive to storage flakiness; they have a regulatory window next week and want a mitigated plan documented. We committed to a temporary local-write fallback and an action plan to replace the problematic node under RMA window.
  - Primary ask: documented failback steps and an ETA for node replacement.
  - Internal owners: Priya (on-site coordination), Marcus (replacement ETA + supplier), Luis (data integrity validation).
- KiteCorp: Non-blocking but noisy; they requested lower-latency tail and network path stability.
  - Primary ask: keep latency under 120ms p95 for control-plane RPCs during peak.

Technical investigation notes (interesting/novel items):
- NFS kernel timeouts on Acadia correlate with bursty IO during nightly backup window. The mount uses vers=4.1 and defaults to rsize/wsize that don't match vendor appliances. Short-term fix: mount tune rsize=65536,wsize=65536 and increase retrans to 3. Long-term: recommend moving state to local NVMe with delayed replication.
- Control-plane GRPC stalls: traced to reassembly/fragmentation at the IPSec tunnel resulting in sporadic retransmits. Path MTU discovery failing due to ICMP rate-limiting on customer firewall. Proposed: MTU clamp + explicit MSS adjustment on tunnel endpoints.
- Installer heuristics: current node-tiling algorithm picks 8 worker processes by default; for small single-rack installs this causes context churn. Patch: make worker count a function of physical CPU sockets and an env var override (PR submitted).

Metrics snapshot (what we measured this week):
- Acadia: token p50 45ms, p95 190ms (baseline p95 ~150ms). Error rate <0.02%. Mount timeouts: 6 events in 48h.
- KiteCorp: control-plane rpc p50 28ms, p95 135ms (target <120ms). IPSec reassembly retrans rate: 0.8% of packets during peak.

Decisions made:
- Canary MTU clamp applied to 10% of KiteCorp traffic for 24h; if p95 improves by >10% we will roll to 50% and then 100% in 48h windows. (Owner: Ethan)
- Add installer prewarm job to reduce cold-start token latency for onprem small clusters. (Owner: Sara)
- Defer heavy refactor of NFS-backed state in favor of hardware replacement RMA for Acadia to meet the regulatory timeline. (Owner: Marcus + Logistics)

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Priya: Collect node-02 dmesg + /var/log/messages and upload diagnostic bundle (due 2026-05-12).
- Ethan: Open DEPLOY-418 with packet captures and proposed MTU clamp steps; coordinate customer netops (due 2026-05-13).
- Sara: Draft prewarm job and smoke-test in staging; open PR for installer changes (due 2026-05-14).
- Luis: Run data-integrity checks post-failover and confirm no missing segments (due 2026-05-13).
- Marcus: Confirm RMA timeline and procurement ETA for replacement node (due 2026-05-14).

Open questions / risks:
- If the replacement node lead time exceeds the regulatory window, we'll need a plan to extend local-write fallback for an additional 7 days — what are the risk thresholds for data drift? (Luis to quantify)
- Is there a durable way to make MTU discovery reliable across customer firewalls that intentionally rate-limit ICMP? (Networking experiment backlog item)
- Are our prewarm synthetic traces representative enough for high-variance customer prompts? Need a small set of customer-derived prompts sanitized for prewarm. (Product/QA involvement)

Notes to self / informal:
- Remember to escalate supplier ETA if not confirmed by 2026-05-13; procurement has alternate supplier list in Confluence (see linked artifacts).
- The current automation patch (worker count heuristic) helps small installs but we need load tests for medium installs (4+ racks) to avoid overcommitting CPU.

Next meeting cadence:
- Daily 09:00 standup (PDT) until Acadia RMA complete.
- Network deep-dive Thursday 11:30 (Ethan + customer netops)

Appendix: quick command snippets and references
- How we collected mount logs: sudo journalctl -u nfs-client.target --since "2 days ago" > acadia-mountlog.txt
- Path MTU clamp example (HAProxy iptables): iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- JIRA tickets: DEPLOY-412 (Acadia storage flakiness), DEPLOY-418 (KiteCorp network investigation)

If anything in here should be promoted to the canonical runbook update, mark it and I'll extract a short doc for the team.

-- Marcus
